saw_lines: Sneaker buyers chase one exact model, check fit on a photo, and reorder the same silhouette in a new colorway.
So the sale is won at the opener, where a buyer decides whether this pair is worth a click.
Your 22 of 24 copy ads open on the same arrivals line, so test three new openers built on your own product, like the Air Jordan IV and New Balance 992.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 12 Oct 2026
points: 22 of 24 copy ads open on “check out the latest arrivals”, so one line bids against itself. Run three new angles from your product, like the Air Jordan IV and New Balance 992, each with its own opening line.

0 of 30 ads are video, so every buyer sees a still image of a shoe. Sneakers sell on fit and motion, which a still cannot show. Shoot three videos of sneakers worn on feet and run them beside your ads.

One exact copy runs in 22 of 24 ads, so the same paragraph reaches the same buyers again. Keep the copy and change the opening line and the creative in each ad, so every audience gets a fresh first sentence.

None of your 30 ads shows a proof number, so first-time buyers have nothing concrete to trust. Collect one real figure, like review count or orders shipped, and put it on the creative of your next batch.

ads_1: Fresh openers built on your sneaker drops, tested against the arrivals line
soc_1: Brand social strategy across Facebook and Instagram, your linked channels
